title: AVG Logistics Ltd - 543910 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: AVG Logistics Q4 FY26 PAT rose 104.78% YoY to INR10.71 crores, helped by a INR21 crore lease-reversal income line that management calls operational.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR176.61 crores (+19.4% YoY), EBITDA INR34.72 crores (+45.21%) at a 19.66% margin, and PAT INR10.71 crores (6.06% margin). For FY26, total income was INR582.48 crores (+5.07%), EBITDA INR112.45 crores (+14.27%, 19.31% margin) and PAT INR26.17 crores (+22.71%, 4.49% margin). Management guided to 15-20% growth in FY27 and capex of INR50 crores plus, after INR60 crores in FY26. Analyst questions centred on a one-time-looking lease reversal gain, the late results release, and new segments (liquid logistics by rail, EV/CNG/LNG fleets, Haldiram contract).

segments.name: Road transportation
segments.commentary: Fleet of more than 3,000 owned and hired vehicles; 100-plus vehicles added in FY26 and a similar number targeted for FY27, including CNG, EV and LNG units.

segments.name: Rail / multi-modal
segments.commentary: Rail-based liquid logistics entered in FY26; two tank trains purchased and a third being sought on lease; a rake is targeted in FY27 and 8-10 trains by 2030.

segments.name: Liquid logistics
segments.commentary: Currently about 180 container tankers, with a target of 1,800 tankers; management cited few competitors in chemical liquid transport.

segments.name: Cold chain, warehousing and supply chain management
segments.commentary: Over 7.41 lakh sq ft of warehousing; new Tahliwal (Himachal) land parcel acquired for warehousing; SCM/3PL work for in-plant supply chains described as good-margin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of 15-20%, in line with management's view of industry growth of about 15-20%.
FY27 capex of INR50 crores plus, after about INR60 crores in FY26, for vehicles and long-term contract fleets.
Vision 2030 uploaded the day before the call, citing INR1,250 crores turnover by 2030.
Carbonlite Logistics (50:50 JV with Baidyanath group, LNG-focused) expected to begin operations within about one month of the call.
Liquid logistics fleet to grow from 180 to 1,800 tankers, via import from China or lease in India.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of about INR60 crores; FY27 capex targeted at INR50 crores plus.
Capex in FY26 funded liquid logistics train (two tank trains bought); a third tank train is being sought on lease.
Over 100 vehicles added in FY26 (CNG, EV, LNG and regular trucks); similar addition targeted in FY27.
Tahliwal (Himachal) land acquired for warehouse capacity, strengthening North India presence.
Bank/NBFC financing of 80-90% of vehicle cost cited; EV/LNG purchases tied to 3-7 year customer contracts.
demand_pricing: Haldiram Nagpur contract: three years, extendable to five, for 100 dedicated vehicles across Maharashtra, Gujarat, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka; a further 100 vehicles may follow in two to three months.
Target segments expanded to beverages, liquor, steel, cement, pharma, chemicals, industrial plants and solar, alongside FMCG.
Fuel: most contracts have fuel escalation clauses; management said customers reprice within about 7-15 days of diesel moves, so impact is limited.
Tata Steel and cement customers cited as demanding green logistics; Nestle India and Ashok Leyland CNG corridor contract signed.
Management said EV trucks currently run about 150-200 km per charge; company is installing intermediate chargers for routes such as Chennai-Bangalore (about 400 km).

qa_highlights.question: What revenue growth is targeted for FY27 and what capex was done in FY26 and planned for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 15-20% growth in FY27 based on order book and pipeline. Capex was about INR60 crores in FY26 and is targeted at INR50 crores plus in FY27, mainly for vehicles and rail/liquid assets.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR21 crore lease-reversal gain recurring or one-time, and will normalised FY26 numbers be published?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it is operational income arising from Ind AS 116 lease accounting on terminated long-term contracts, with PwC opinion cited. He called it recurring in nature because the company enters multiple leases regularly, and said it has no tax impact. No normalised numbers were offered.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Q4 results delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed the delay to procedural and audit requirements, with extra reviews and branch consolidation as the business grew. He said the company will aim to stay within statutory timelines.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of rising diesel prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most contracts have fuel escalation clauses, so customers pass through increases within about 7-15 days; some days of cost are absorbed.

qa_highlights.question: Is EV trucking viable for long-haul routes, and how does EV economics compare with diesel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EVs have higher asset cost but much lower operating and maintenance costs, so EV profitability is better when a 3-7 year contract is in place; charging infrastructure is being added on routes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Baidyanath venture?
qa_highlights.answer: Carbonlite Logistics Pvt Ltd is a 50:50 JV with Baidyanath group's LNG arm, to run LNG vehicles on long-term green logistics contracts; operations expected within about a month.

risks_watch: INR21.19 crore lease-reversal income in Q4 FY26 boosts PAT; the company calls it operational, but a sceptical analyst questioned recurrence. Watch Q1 FY27 for underlying margin without it.
Results were released late due to audit reviews; governance and timeliness of future filings to watch.
Fleet expansion and rail assets are debt-funded (80-90% of vehicle cost), so interest and depreciation rise with capex of INR50 crores plus.
EV and LNG economics depend on long-term contracts (3-7 years) and on charging infrastructure for long routes.
Tanker target of 1,800 vehicles depends on imports or leases; execution pace not quantified.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, targets and new segments, with long-run vision statements. Less precise on the lease-reversal accounting and the results delay, where answers were defensive and repeated the statutory-requirement and auditor-opinion points.
key_quotes: Based on our current order book, customer pipeline, and expansion into new business segment, we expect to deliver healthy double-digit revenue growth in FY27.
This is not a windfall profit and it is very well the whatever adjustment entry as per the Ind AS requirement we are doing in the P&L, it has the impact of that.
My vehicle is earning from the day one.

growth.why: Management targets 15-20% FY27 revenue growth (midpoint 17.5%), backed by 100+ planned vehicle additions, an LNG JV starting within a month, a targeted FY27 rake and Haldiram's 100-vehicle contract, but the 180-to-1,800 tanker plan has no timeline and the rake and warehouse are not yet built.
